title: Run a structured stakeholder listening tour
description: Meet the CEO, every functional leader, the lead director, and the two or three managers who actually produce finance data. Use the same question set for each conversation so answers can be compared rather than remembered.
outcome: A written summary of what each stakeholder needs from finance, what they think is broken, and where their view conflicts with another leader's view.
recommendationReason: A new CFO who diagnoses before acting avoids rebuilding the wrong thing first. Comparable notes surface conflicts that private conversations hide.
deliverables: Stakeholder map with influence and dependency notes
Top ten themes with conflicting views flagged

title: Assess the finance function end to end
description: Score the current state of close, controls, planning, systems, treasury, tax, and team against a written maturity rubric. Record what exists, what is undocumented, and what is a single point of failure.
outcome: A baseline maturity score by area with the five gaps that create the most risk in the next two quarters.
recommendationReason: Every later decision about hiring, systems, and sequencing depends on an honest baseline taken before the new CFO is captured by day-to-day work.
deliverables: Finance maturity assessment scored by area

title: Verify cash, burn, and runway independently
description: Pull bank balances directly from each institution, tie them to the general ledger, recompute net burn for the last six months, and restate runway. Do not accept the number in the last board deck without proving it.
outcome: A cash and runway figure the CFO has personally verified, with a written explanation of any difference from the previously reported number.
recommendationReason: Runway is the single number a CFO cannot be wrong about. Verifying it in week one prevents inheriting someone else's error.

title: Diagnose the close and management reporting cycle
description: Sit through or reconstruct the last close. Time each step, find where the delay actually is, and list every manual adjustment made after the trial balance was produced.
outcome: A close timeline with the three steps that create most of the delay, and a list of post-close manual adjustments that indicate control gaps.
recommendationReason: Close cycle time and manual top-side entries are the fastest read on accounting quality and on where the controller gap sits.
deliverables: Manual journal entry log with explanations
Reporting distribution list and delivery dates

title: Inventory finance systems, data flows, and spend
description: List every system that touches money: accounting, billing, payroll, expense, procurement, banking, equity, and the spreadsheets holding it all together. Record owner, cost, renewal date, and how data moves between them.
outcome: One page showing which systems exist, who owns each, what they cost, and which handoffs are manual.
recommendationReason: Systems decisions later in the year are cheaper and faster when the starting architecture and contract renewal dates are already documented.
deliverables: Finance systems inventory with owners and renewal dates
Data flow diagram showing manual handoffs

title: Assess team skills, capacity, and retention risk
description: Map current roles against the work the function actually has to perform. Identify who is overloaded, who is underused, who is a flight risk, and which capabilities are missing entirely.
outcome: A team map showing coverage by capability, named retention risks, and the capability gaps that must be hired or outsourced.
recommendationReason: Hiring sequence and outsourcing choices depend on knowing which capabilities the current team can genuinely cover.
deliverables: Retention risk list with mitigation notes

title: Review board history, commitments, and investor expectations
description: Read the last four board decks, minutes, consents, the financing documents, and the most recent investor updates. Build a list of every commitment made to the board and its current status.
outcome: A commitment register that shows what the board was promised, by when, and whether it is on track.
recommendationReason: Inherited commitments are the most common source of early credibility damage because the new CFO does not know they exist.
deliverables: Summary of protective provisions and consent rights

title: Deliver a 30-day findings readout to the CEO
description: Present what is working, what is at risk, what will be fixed first, and what will deliberately wait. Ask for explicit agreement on the top three priorities and on what finance will stop doing.
outcome: Written CEO agreement on the top three finance priorities and on the work finance will not take on this quarter.
recommendationReason: Explicit priority agreement in month one prevents the finance team from being pulled in five directions by month three.

title: Design the finance operating model
description: Decide what finance does centrally, what it embeds with business partners, what it outsources, and what it automates. Write it down as a target model with a rough cost per option.
outcome: A written target operating model with owner, delivery method, and cost for each finance capability.
recommendationReason: Hiring, outsourcing, and systems spend should all follow one operating model decision rather than being decided case by case.
deliverables: Build, buy, or outsource decision per capability

title: Publish the finance 90-day plan
description: Turn the agreed priorities into a dated plan with named owners, weekly checkpoints, and a short definition of done for each item. Share it with the executive team, not only with finance.
outcome: A published 90-day plan that other functions can see, plan around, and hold finance to.
recommendationReason: A visible plan converts CFO intent into cross-functional expectations and makes slippage obvious early.

title: Build the finance hiring plan and sequence
description: Sequence hires against the operating model and the calendar of work. Controller coverage comes first when it is not full-time, then strategic finance, then accounting or systems capacity based on measured workload.
outcome: An approved hiring sequence with budget, target start dates, and the trigger that justifies each role.
recommendationReason: Hiring out of sequence is the most expensive mistake a new finance leader makes. The controller gap blocks close, audit, and controls work simultaneously.
deliverables: Hiring sequence with triggers and target dates
Interim coverage plan for unfilled roles

title: Agree service levels with other functions
description: Write down what finance delivers to sales, engineering, marketing, and people operations, when it delivers it, and what those teams must provide in return for it to happen on time.
outcome: Signed service expectations that make finance dependencies explicit in both directions.
recommendationReason: Most late finance deliverables are caused by late inputs from other teams. Written expectations move that conversation before the deadline.

title: Publish the annual finance calendar
description: Combine close dates, reporting deadlines, board meetings, planning cycles, audit milestones, tax deadlines, payroll dates, and equity events into one calendar everyone can subscribe to.
outcome: A single published calendar that shows every recurring finance date for the next twelve months.
recommendationReason: One calendar removes the constant scheduling negotiation and makes capacity conflicts visible months ahead.
deliverables: Shared calendar subscription for the executive team

title: Own the first full board meeting as CFO
description: Take control of the financial narrative: agreed numbers, an honest read on the plan, the two or three decisions the board must make, and a clear statement of what finance is fixing.
outcome: A board meeting where the numbers are not debated, the decisions are framed, and the CFO's credibility is established.
recommendationReason: The first board meeting sets the standard for every later one. Framing decisions rather than reporting history changes how the board uses finance.

title: Publish the finance charter and ownership matrix
description: Document what finance owns, what it partners on, and what it only advises. Assign a named owner and a named backup to every recurring finance responsibility.
outcome: A charter that removes ambiguity about who decides what, with backup coverage named for every critical process.
recommendationReason: Ownership ambiguity is the main reason finance work falls between roles during busy periods.

title: Review vendor and discretionary spend
description: Rank every vendor by annual spend, check usage against licenses, find duplicate tools, and identify contracts renewing in the next six months where leverage still exists.
outcome: A ranked savings list with named owners and renewal dates, sized against the current burn plan.
recommendationReason: Vendor spend is usually the fastest source of burn reduction that does not touch headcount or roadmap.
deliverables: Renewal action plan with target savings

title: Launch a finance function scorecard
description: Measure the finance team itself: close days, reconciliation completion, forecast accuracy, days sales outstanding, on-time filings, and open audit items. Report it monthly like any other function.
outcome: A monthly finance scorecard that makes the function's own performance visible and improvable.
recommendationReason: Finance holds every other function to metrics. Applying the same standard internally builds credibility and drives real improvement.

title: Build succession and bench coverage
description: For each critical finance process, name a trained backup, document the process well enough for that backup to run it, and test the handoff at least once.
outcome: No finance process depends on one person being available.
recommendationReason: Key-person dependency in finance becomes a diligence finding and an operating failure at the worst possible moment.

title: Refresh the finance strategy for the coming year
description: Reassess the operating model against actual scale, next year's plan, and the likely financing path. Decide what to automate, insource, outsource, or stop doing.
outcome: An updated finance strategy and budget aligned to next year's operating plan and capital plan.
recommendationReason: The operating model designed for the current scale rarely fits the next one. Reviewing it annually keeps cost and capability aligned.

title: Build a benchmarking and peer network
description: Establish a small set of comparable companies and trusted peer CFOs to test benchmarks for close days, finance headcount ratio, spend per employee, and gross margin structure.
outcome: External reference points that let the CFO judge whether internal metrics are actually good.
recommendationReason: Internal metrics without external comparison invite either complacency or unnecessary alarm.

title: Run the weekly finance leadership meeting
description: A short standing meeting with a fixed agenda: cash, blockers, close or forecast status, hiring, and one decision. Written notes and owners published the same day.
outcome: Weekly written decisions and owners, with blockers escalated before they become misses.
recommendationReason: A fixed weekly rhythm is what keeps a small finance team synchronized without constant ad hoc meetings.

title: Run the monthly business review with the executive team
description: Present actuals against plan, the updated forecast, the KPI movement that matters, and the decisions required. Keep the historical reporting short and spend the time on decisions.
outcome: A monthly executive decision meeting anchored on one set of numbers.
recommendationReason: Without a standing review, financial results are discussed only when something goes wrong, which is too late to change the outcome.

title: Standardize the monthly executive reporting pack
description: Fix the format, the metric definitions, the delivery date, and the distribution list for the monthly pack so it never has to be renegotiated.
outcome: A repeatable monthly pack delivered on a committed date in a consistent format.
recommendationReason: A stable reporting format lets readers compare months instead of relearning the deck each time.

title: Hold quarterly development conversations with the finance team
description: Every quarter, review each team member's goals, growth areas, workload, and career direction. Record commitments and revisit them the following quarter.
outcome: Documented development plans that reduce attrition and build the internal bench.
recommendationReason: Finance teams at this stage lose people to burnout and unclear growth paths more often than to compensation.

title: Run the annual finance performance and compensation cycle
description: Complete reviews, calibrate ratings against the rest of the company, set next-year goals, and process compensation and equity decisions within the approved budget.
outcome: Calibrated reviews and funded compensation decisions delivered on the company cycle.
recommendationReason: Finance leaders who run their own cycle late lose credibility when they enforce deadlines on others.

title: Baseline the monthly close process
description: Document every close step, who performs it, what system it touches, how long it takes, and which steps depend on an input from outside finance. Measure the actual working days to a locked trial balance.
outcome: A step-level close map with measured cycle time and the dependencies that drive the critical path.
recommendationReason: Close cycle time cannot be improved before the current steps and their true dependencies are written down and measured.

title: Review every balance sheet account for support
description: Go line by line through the balance sheet and confirm each balance is supported by a reconciliation, a schedule, or a third-party statement. Flag anything unsupported, stale, or unexplained.
outcome: A schedule showing which balance sheet accounts are supported, which are not, and the size of the unsupported balances.
recommendationReason: Unsupported balance sheet balances are where inherited errors hide and where the first audit will focus.

title: Build the accounting clean-up log
description: Collect every known accounting issue: unreconciled differences, suspense accounts, aged accruals, unapplied cash, and prior-period adjustments. Size each one and rank by risk.
outcome: One ranked clean-up log with amounts, owners, and target resolution dates.
recommendationReason: A single ranked log prevents clean-up work from being rediscovered every close and lets the CFO judge audit exposure.
deliverables: Clean-up log with amounts and owners

title: Review the current revenue recognition policy and practice
description: Compare what the written revenue policy says with what the billing system and the general ledger actually do. Test a sample of contracts across each contract type and pricing structure.
outcome: A written assessment of whether recorded revenue follows the stated policy, with every difference documented.
recommendationReason: Revenue is the highest-risk area in a first audit and the hardest to restate later. Testing early keeps remediation cheap.

title: Check accounting system configuration and data quality
description: Review the chart of accounts structure, dimension usage, posting rules, open periods, user permissions, and the volume of manual journal entries relative to automated postings.
outcome: A configuration assessment showing where the system is being worked around rather than used.
recommendationReason: Heavy manual journal entry volume is a reliable signal that system configuration, not staffing, is the constraint.

title: Publish a close calendar and task checklist
description: Convert the close map into a dated calendar with named owners, preparer and reviewer for each task, and hard cut-off times for inputs from payroll, billing, and expense.
outcome: A published close calendar where every task has an owner, a reviewer, and a due day.
recommendationReason: A close without published owners and cut-offs runs on memory and slips whenever one person is unavailable.
deliverables: Task checklist with preparer and reviewer

title: Redesign the chart of accounts and dimensions
description: Rebuild the account structure so it supports gross margin reporting, department and cost center analysis, and the metric definitions the board sees. Use dimensions rather than proliferating accounts.
outcome: A dimensioned chart of accounts that produces management reporting directly from the ledger.
recommendationReason: A chart of accounts built for tax filing rather than management reporting forces every analysis into spreadsheets.
deliverables: New chart of accounts with mapping from old accounts

title: Set reconciliation standards and templates
description: Define which accounts require monthly reconciliation, the template to use, the supporting evidence required, the reviewer, and the threshold above which a difference must be explained and cleared.
outcome: A standard reconciliation package with defined preparer, reviewer, and clearance thresholds.
recommendationReason: Consistent reconciliation format is what makes review possible at speed and gives the auditor a repeatable evidence trail.
deliverables: Account risk ranking and required frequency

title: Write the accrual and cut-off policy
description: Set materiality thresholds for accruals, define the standard recurring accruals, document estimation methods, and fix cut-off rules for invoices, expenses, payroll, and revenue.
outcome: Written accrual and cut-off rules that produce consistent results regardless of who performs the close.
recommendationReason: Inconsistent accrual judgment is the leading cause of month-to-month volatility that nobody can explain in the flux review.

title: Build the accounting policy manual
description: Write the company's accounting positions in one document: revenue, capitalization, leases, stock compensation, prepaid expenses, reserves, foreign currency, and materiality.
outcome: One approved policy manual that the team, the auditor, and any new hire can work from.
recommendationReason: Auditors ask for written policy first. Writing it before the audit turns a scramble into a document review.

title: Reduce close cycle time to the target
description: Attack the critical path: pre-close the recurring items, automate the repetitive journals, move reconciliations before day one, and set a hard cut-off that other functions must meet.
outcome: A close that lands on the committed day count for two consecutive months without heroics.
recommendationReason: A long close delays every downstream decision and consumes the capacity needed for analysis and controls work.
deliverables: Revised close calendar with target days
Two months of measured close results

title: Standardize monthly flux analysis
description: Require a written explanation for every account movement above a set threshold, prepared during close rather than after it, and reviewed before the books are locked.
outcome: Every material movement is explained before the numbers are published, not after someone asks.
recommendationReason: Flux analysis performed during close catches errors while they can still be corrected in the same period.
deliverables: Review sign-off step in the close checklist

title: Write or refresh the revenue recognition memo
description: Document the five-step analysis for each revenue stream, including performance obligations, variable consideration, standalone selling price, principal versus agent conclusions, and contract cost treatment.
outcome: An auditor-ready revenue memo covering every revenue stream the company sells today.
recommendationReason: Revenue memos written under audit pressure are weaker and more expensive than memos written from the current contract set.

title: Control revenue recognition for usage-based pricing
description: Tie metered usage data to invoices and to recognized revenue, define the treatment of unbilled usage and overage, and build a completeness check on the usage feed itself.
outcome: Usage revenue that reconciles from raw metering data through invoicing to the general ledger.
recommendationReason: Usage pricing moves the revenue completeness risk upstream into engineering-owned metering data that finance does not control.

title: Establish fixed asset and capitalization discipline
description: Set capitalization thresholds, build or rebuild the fixed asset register, verify useful lives and depreciation methods, and reconcile the register to the general ledger.
outcome: A fixed asset register that agrees to the ledger with documented lives and thresholds.
recommendationReason: Fixed asset registers drift quickly when purchases are approved by several teams and nobody owns the register.
deliverables: Fixed asset register reconciled to the ledger

title: Build the intercompany and consolidation process
description: Define intercompany transaction types, agree the settlement cadence, set the elimination entries, define currency translation treatment, and build a repeatable consolidation workbook or system process.
outcome: A consolidation that runs from subsidiary trial balances to consolidated statements with documented eliminations.
recommendationReason: Multiple entities without a defined consolidation process produce intercompany differences that grow every month.

title: Tighten accounts payable accounting and controls
description: Enforce purchase approval before invoice entry, three-way matching where goods are received, coding standards, duplicate invoice detection, and a documented payment release approval.
outcome: Payables that are approved before they are entered and paid only through a controlled release process.
recommendationReason: Payables is the most common fraud and error path in a growing company because approval and payment often sit with the same person.
deliverables: Approval matrix mapped into the payables system

title: Define the billing to accounts receivable handoff
description: Agree who creates the invoice, who approves non-standard terms, how the billing system posts to the ledger, how credits and refunds are approved, and how unapplied cash is cleared.
outcome: A documented handoff where every invoice traces to an approved order and every receipt is applied within the month.
recommendationReason: Billing errors damage customer trust and distort revenue, and they usually come from an undefined boundary between sales operations and accounting.

title: Prepare audit readiness and the requested items list
description: Build the audit request list before the auditor sends it. Assign each item an owner and a due date, and pre-populate the workpapers that are predictable every year.
outcome: An audit that starts with most requested items already prepared and indexed.
recommendationReason: Audit cost and duration are driven mostly by how quickly requested items are delivered and how well the support is organized.

title: Select an audit firm and agree scope
description: Run a short competitive process, compare firm experience with the business model, confirm partner and manager continuity, and negotiate scope, fees, and the timeline before signing.
outcome: A signed engagement with a firm that has done this business model before and a timeline that fits the close calendar.
recommendationReason: The first audit sets precedent for every later one, and firm fit matters more than headline fee.

title: Build the technical accounting memo library
description: Create a standard memo format and write memos for every judgment area: revenue, capitalized software, leases, stock compensation, reserves, business combinations, and any unusual transaction.
outcome: A memo library that documents each significant judgment with the analysis and conclusion recorded at the time.
recommendationReason: Judgments explained from memory two years later are worth far less than judgments documented when the transaction happened.
deliverables: Completed memos for open judgment areas

title: Implement lease accounting
description: Inventory every lease including office space, equipment, and embedded leases in service contracts. Build the right-of-use asset and liability schedules and the recurring journal entries.
outcome: A complete lease schedule with balance sheet recognition and repeatable monthly entries.
recommendationReason: Leases are frequently incomplete because embedded leases inside service agreements are missed until the auditor finds them.

title: Implement stock compensation accounting
description: Value grants, set the forfeiture approach, build the expense amortization schedule, reconcile it to the cap table system, and produce the disclosure roll-forward.
outcome: Stock compensation expense that reconciles to the cap table and rolls forward correctly each period.
recommendationReason: Stock compensation expense that does not tie to the cap table is a common and time-consuming audit finding.

title: Set the capitalized software policy and process
description: Define which development stages qualify, how engineering time is captured and allocated, the approval required, and the amortization period. Build the recurring calculation.
outcome: A defensible capitalized software calculation supported by time data rather than estimates made after the fact.
recommendationReason: Software capitalization moves real expense between periods, so the method must be documented and consistently applied.
deliverables: Capitalization policy for internal-use and external software

title: Structure cost of revenue and infrastructure cost accounting
description: Define what belongs in cost of revenue for compute, model inference, data, hosting, and support. Build allocation rules so gross margin can be reported by product and by customer segment.
outcome: A cost of revenue structure that produces credible gross margin by product without manual rework.
recommendationReason: Infrastructure-heavy business models cannot report meaningful gross margin until compute and inference costs are classified and allocated consistently.

title: Run the annual audit to completion
description: Manage fieldwork, deliver requested items on schedule, resolve findings, respond to proposed adjustments, and finish with signed statements and a management letter response.
outcome: Signed financial statements with no material adjustments and a written response to every management letter point.
recommendationReason: Audit execution quality determines diligence speed in the next financing and the level of scrutiny in future audits.

title: Convert the books fully to accrual accounting standards
description: Where the books still carry cash-basis or simplified treatments, convert them, restate comparative periods, and document the differences for the board and the auditor.
outcome: Books prepared under one consistent accounting framework with restated comparatives.
recommendationReason: Mixed accounting bases make period comparison meaningless and are always discovered during diligence.

title: Automate recurring close work
description: Move recurring journals, reconciliation matching, accrual calculations, and flux commentary collection into tooling. Retire the spreadsheets that only one person understands.
outcome: A measurable reduction in manual close hours with the same or better accuracy.
recommendationReason: Automating the repetitive parts of close is what allows the accounting team to grow revenue coverage without growing headcount at the same rate.
deliverables: Automation candidate list with hours saved

title: Execute the monthly close
description: Run the close to the published calendar: cut-off, subledger closes, accruals, reconciliations, flux review, management review, and lock the period.
outcome: Locked books and published financial statements on the committed day each month.
recommendationReason: A predictable close is the foundation every other finance deliverable depends on.

title: Complete and review monthly reconciliations
description: Prepare every required reconciliation, have a second person review it, clear aged differences, and escalate anything above the threshold that cannot be cleared.
outcome: All required accounts reconciled and reviewed before the period is locked.
recommendationReason: Reconciliations completed after the period is locked cannot prevent the error from being reported.

title: Review payables and receivables subledgers weekly
description: Check aged payables and receivables, unapplied cash, credit memos issued, and any invoice held in error before the amounts age into the close.
outcome: Subledger issues are found and fixed during the month rather than during close.
recommendationReason: Weekly subledger review keeps close-week surprises out of the critical path.

title: Review technical accounting positions quarterly
description: Revisit judgment areas for new contract types, new products, new geographies, and any standard-setting change that affects the company's positions.
outcome: Accounting positions stay current with the business instead of being revisited only at audit.
recommendationReason: New products and contract structures are introduced faster than accounting policy is updated unless a review is scheduled.

title: Prepare annual financial statements and disclosures
description: Produce the full annual statements with footnotes, related party disclosures, commitments, subsequent events, and the supporting disclosure checklist.
outcome: Complete annual statements with disclosures ready for the auditor and the board.
recommendationReason: Disclosure preparation is consistently underestimated and is a common cause of audit delay.

title: Review non-standard contracts for accounting impact
description: Any contract with unusual terms, non-standard payment schedules, performance commitments, or bundled deliverables gets an accounting review before signature.
outcome: Accounting treatment is agreed before the contract is signed rather than discovered at close.
recommendationReason: Terms agreed in a deal room become accounting problems that cannot be renegotiated after signature.
deliverables: Contract review note with accounting conclusion

title: Define the error and restatement protocol
description: Write the process for evaluating an identified error: materiality assessment, correction method, communication to the audit committee, and documentation requirements.
outcome: A defined path for handling accounting errors that does not depend on improvisation under pressure.
recommendationReason: Errors are handled better and faster when the evaluation and escalation path was agreed before one was found.

title: Audit the existing financial model
description: Trace the current model from revenue drivers to cash. Test the formulas, find hardcoded values inside calculations, check whether actuals tie to the ledger, and decide whether to repair or rebuild.
outcome: A written verdict on the model with the specific defects found and a repair or rebuild decision.
recommendationReason: Every planning conversation in the first quarter runs through this model, so its defects must be known before it is used to make commitments.

title: Inventory KPIs and find conflicting definitions
description: Collect every metric used in board decks, executive dashboards, sales reporting, and investor updates. Compare the definitions and identify where the same metric name carries different meanings.
outcome: A list of every metric in use with each conflicting definition documented and a proposed single definition.
recommendationReason: Conflicting metric definitions destroy trust in reporting faster than errors do, because nobody can tell which number is wrong.

title: Normalize historical actuals for analysis
description: Build a clean monthly history of revenue, gross margin, operating expense by department, headcount, and cash. Remove one-time items and reclassifications so trends are comparable.
outcome: A comparable multi-year monthly actuals dataset that ties to the general ledger.
recommendationReason: Forecasts built on inconsistent history inherit the inconsistency and produce trends that do not exist.

title: Build the integrated three-statement model
description: Build a driver-based model where the income statement, balance sheet, and cash flow statement connect, working capital behaves realistically, and every assumption sits on a single input sheet.
outcome: One model that produces all three statements from documented drivers with no hardcoded values inside calculations.
recommendationReason: Runway, hiring, and pricing decisions all require a model where cash follows from the operating assumptions rather than being estimated separately.

title: Publish the KPI dictionary
description: For each approved metric, write the definition, the formula, the source system, the owner, the reporting frequency, and any known limitation. Get executive agreement before publishing.
outcome: One published dictionary that every report, dashboard, and board deck must follow.
recommendationReason: A published dictionary ends recurring arguments about whose number is right and makes reporting reproducible.

title: Stand up budget versus actual reporting
description: Load the current budget into the reporting system at the same level of detail as actuals, and produce variance reporting by department with written explanations from budget owners.
outcome: Monthly variance reporting by department where the owner, not finance, explains the variance.
recommendationReason: Variance explained by finance is a report. Variance explained by the budget owner is accountability.
deliverables: Budget loaded to the reporting system

title: Build the driver-based headcount and compensation model
description: Model headcount by role, location, start date, and fully loaded cost including taxes, benefits, and equipment. Link it to the operating expense forecast so hiring changes flow through automatically.
outcome: A headcount model where changing a start date updates the expense forecast and the runway without manual rework.
recommendationReason: People cost is the largest expense line at this stage, so the plan is only as good as the headcount model behind it.
deliverables: Headcount model with fully loaded cost

title: Establish the rolling forecast process
description: Set a monthly forecast cycle with a fixed input deadline, business partner review, a documented change log, and a comparison of the new forecast to the prior one and to plan.
outcome: A monthly forecast that is updated on schedule and whose changes are explained rather than silently absorbed.
recommendationReason: An annual budget alone goes stale within a quarter at this growth rate, and stale numbers drive late decisions.

title: Build the scenario and sensitivity framework
description: Define base, upside, and downside cases with explicit trigger conditions, and build sensitivity analysis on the drivers that move runway most: growth rate, gross margin, hiring pace, and collections.
outcome: Three defensible scenarios with named triggers and a sensitivity view showing which drivers actually matter.
recommendationReason: Boards make better decisions when the downside case and its triggers are already defined instead of built during a crisis.

title: Design the board analytics package
description: Standardize the analytical section of the board package: growth and retention, unit economics, efficiency, cash and runway, plan performance, and the specific decisions being requested.
outcome: A consistent board analytics format that lets directors compare quarters and focus on decisions.
recommendationReason: Board packages that change format every quarter force directors to relearn the story and hide trend deterioration.
deliverables: Data source mapping for each exhibit

title: Build cohort and retention analytics
description: Build revenue and logo retention by cohort, gross and net revenue retention, expansion and contraction decomposition, and churn reasons where available.
outcome: Cohort analysis that shows whether the business is compounding or refilling a leaking bucket.
recommendationReason: Retention by cohort is the metric investors test hardest and the one most often computed inconsistently.

title: Decompose gross margin by product and segment
description: Break gross margin into its components, allocate shared infrastructure and support cost, and show margin by product, plan tier, and customer segment over time.
outcome: Gross margin reported at a level where pricing and cost decisions can actually be made.
recommendationReason: Blended gross margin hides which products are subsidizing others and delays pricing action.
deliverables: Margin trend by product and segment

title: Enable department budget owners
description: Give each budget owner a live view of their spend, a simple forecast input process, training on how their decisions flow to the plan, and a clear approval threshold.
outcome: Budget owners who manage their own numbers instead of asking finance what they spent.
recommendationReason: Central budget control does not scale past a certain headcount and slows every purchasing decision.

title: Create the capital allocation framework
description: Define how investment requests are evaluated: required return or payback, strategic fit, risk, and the approval threshold. Require the same format for every request.
outcome: A consistent framework so investment decisions are compared on the same basis.
recommendationReason: Without a shared framework, capital goes to the most persuasive advocate rather than the highest return.

title: Build the annual operating plan
description: Run the full planning cycle: strategic targets from the CEO and board, bottom-up department plans, reconciliation of the gap, scenario testing, and board approval.
outcome: A board-approved operating plan with department budgets, a headcount plan, and cash targets everyone has signed up to.
recommendationReason: The annual plan is the contract between the board, the executive team, and every department for the year.

title: Build the three-year long range plan
description: Extend the model to a multi-year view showing the path to target margins, the capital required, and the milestones that must be hit for the next financing to be raised on good terms.
outcome: A multi-year view that connects the current plan to the next financing and to profitability.
recommendationReason: Investors at the next round evaluate the multi-year path, so it should be built before the fundraising conversation starts.
deliverables: Milestone map to the next financing

title: Prepare the fundraising model and diligence support
description: Build the investor-facing model, the metrics package, the cohort and unit economics support, and the historical tie-outs that diligence will request. Anticipate the hard questions and answer them in the materials.
outcome: A fundraising model and data package that survives investor diligence without last-minute rebuilds.
recommendationReason: Diligence questions arrive faster than they can be answered from scratch, and slow answers are read as weak controls.

title: Build the acquisition and partnership analysis playbook
description: Create a standard approach for evaluating an acquisition, a large partnership, or a build versus buy decision: valuation method, integration cost, synergy tests, and the diligence checklist.
outcome: A repeatable evaluation method so opportunistic deals are assessed consistently rather than emotionally.
recommendationReason: Acquisition opportunities appear with short deadlines, and the analysis framework should exist before one does.

title: Analyze efficiency metrics against benchmarks
description: Measure revenue per employee, spend by function as a share of revenue, sales efficiency, and burn multiple, and compare against relevant peer benchmarks by stage and business model.
outcome: An efficiency analysis that identifies where the company is out of line with comparable businesses.
recommendationReason: Efficiency metrics drive valuation and investor conviction more than growth alone at this stage.

title: Run the mid-year plan reset
description: Compare year-to-date performance with the plan, decide whether to reforecast or hold the plan, and reset targets, hiring pace, and spend authority accordingly with board visibility.
outcome: A documented mid-year decision on whether the plan still stands, with adjusted targets where it does not.
recommendationReason: Holding an unreachable plan for a full year destroys the credibility of the planning process and delays corrective action.

title: Publish the weekly KPI flash report
description: Distribute a short weekly report with the handful of metrics that move weekly: bookings, pipeline, cash, usage or activity, and hiring, each against target.
outcome: The executive team sees the same short set of leading indicators every week.
recommendationReason: Weekly leading indicators surface problems while there is still time in the quarter to respond.

title: Update the rolling forecast monthly
description: Load actuals, refresh drivers, collect business partner input, update the forecast, and document what changed and why relative to the prior version.
outcome: A current forecast every month with an auditable explanation of each change.
recommendationReason: Forecast changes that are not explained get treated as noise and the forecast stops influencing decisions.

title: Run the monthly budget variance review
description: Meet each budget owner group, review variance against plan and forecast, capture written explanations, and agree corrective actions with dates.
outcome: Variances are explained and acted on by owners within days of close.
recommendationReason: Variance reporting without a review meeting produces explanations but no behavior change.

title: Produce quarterly board materials
description: Build the board package on the standard format, circulate a pre-read several days ahead, and prepare the decision memos for anything requiring board approval.
outcome: A board package delivered as a pre-read with decisions framed before the meeting.
recommendationReason: Board packages delivered at the meeting turn the meeting into a reading session instead of a decision session.

title: Run the annual planning cycle
description: Manage the full cycle each year: calendar, targets, bottom-up submissions, reconciliation, scenario review, board approval, and loading the approved budget into the systems.
outcome: An approved budget loaded into the reporting system before the first day of the new year.
recommendationReason: Planning cycles that finish after the year begins force a quarter of decisions to be made against last year's budget.

title: Review investment business cases as they arise
description: Any request above the approval threshold gets a standard business case: cost, expected return, payback, risks, and the decision recommendation.
outcome: Investment decisions above threshold are documented with the analysis that supported them.
recommendationReason: Ad hoc investment approvals leave no record of what was promised, which prevents any later accountability.

title: Baseline bookings, pipeline, and revenue data quality
description: Reconcile the customer relationship system to billing and to the ledger. Test whether closed-won amounts match signed contracts and whether pipeline stages and close dates are maintained honestly.
outcome: A documented view of how reliable the commercial data is and where it breaks.
recommendationReason: Every commercial analysis depends on this data, and at this stage it usually disagrees with the ledger by a material amount.
deliverables: Stage and close date hygiene assessment

title: Establish the unit economics baseline
description: Compute customer acquisition cost, payback period, lifetime value, and gross margin per customer using consistent definitions and fully loaded costs. Document every assumption.
outcome: A defensible unit economics baseline with assumptions written down and testable.
recommendationReason: Unit economics quoted from an old deck are usually optimistic, and the board will test them at the next financing.

title: Review pricing and packaging
description: Analyze realized price against list, discount depth by segment and by representative, win rates by price point, and whether the packaging tiers still match how customers buy.
outcome: A pricing assessment showing where value is being given away and where price can move.
recommendationReason: Pricing is the fastest lever on gross margin, and packaging set at an earlier stage rarely fits the current customer base.
deliverables: Discount depth and win rate analysis

title: Stand up the deal desk
description: Create a single path for non-standard deals: submission format, required approvals, response time commitment, and a written record of what was approved and why.
outcome: Non-standard deals are reviewed by finance before signature with a documented approval trail.
recommendationReason: Non-standard terms agreed without finance review become revenue recognition problems and collection problems later.
deliverables: Deal desk process and submission form

title: Set the discount and terms approval matrix
description: Define what a sales representative can approve alone, what needs a manager, what needs the CFO, and what needs the CEO, covering discount, payment terms, contract length, and service commitments.
outcome: Clear approval limits that let standard deals close quickly and route only the exceptions.
recommendationReason: Without published limits, every deal becomes an escalation and the exception becomes the norm.

title: Map and fix the quote-to-cash process
description: Trace a deal from quote through order form, signature, provisioning, invoice, collection, and revenue recognition. Find every manual re-keying step and every place data is re-entered.
outcome: A process map with the specific handoffs that cause billing errors and collection delays.
recommendationReason: Most billing disputes and days sales outstanding problems begin as a broken handoff between selling and billing.

title: Review sales commission plans and calculations
description: Check that plans pay on the behavior the company wants, that the calculation is reproducible, that accrual treatment is correct, and that disputes are rare and resolved quickly.
outcome: Commission plans that are affordable, calculable, and aligned to margin rather than volume alone.
recommendationReason: Commission plans drive representative behavior more than any strategy document, and calculation errors destroy sales trust fast.

title: Build the collections strategy
description: Segment receivables by risk and size, define the outreach sequence and timing, agree escalation to the account owner, set credit hold rules, and measure days sales outstanding weekly.
outcome: A collections process with defined ownership and escalation that measurably reduces days sales outstanding.
recommendationReason: Collections is the cheapest source of cash available and is usually run informally until someone owns it.

title: Build the go-to-market capacity and quota model
description: Model representative ramp time, productivity by tenure, territory coverage, quota coverage ratio, and the hiring lead time required to hit next year's bookings target.
outcome: A capacity model that shows whether the bookings plan is achievable with the planned sales headcount.
recommendationReason: Bookings plans fail most often because hiring and ramp math was never done, not because the market changed.

title: Build revenue assurance for usage-based billing
description: Verify that metered events are complete, correctly rated, correctly invoiced, and correctly recognized. Build automated checks for missing usage, mis-rated records, and unbilled consumption.
outcome: Confidence that consumption delivered is consumption billed, with exceptions detected automatically.
recommendationReason: Usage pricing places revenue completeness inside engineering systems, which is the single largest revenue leakage risk in this model.

title: Analyze customer-level profitability
description: Allocate direct delivery cost, infrastructure consumption, and support effort to individual customers to find which accounts are unprofitable at current pricing.
outcome: A ranked view of customer profitability that supports renewal pricing and support model decisions.
recommendationReason: A small number of heavy-usage accounts frequently consume most of the infrastructure cost while paying an average price.

title: Formalize the acquisition cost and payback framework
description: Standardize how sales and marketing cost is attributed to new versus expansion business, compute blended and paid payback separately, and set the efficiency targets the plan assumes.
outcome: One agreed method for measuring acquisition efficiency that finance, marketing, and the board all use.
recommendationReason: Acquisition cost computed differently by each function makes it impossible to judge whether spending more is working.
deliverables: Payback calculation by channel and segment

title: Build renewal and expansion analytics
description: Build the renewal forecast from contract dates, model renewal likelihood using usage and support signals, and track expansion pipeline separately from new business.
outcome: A renewal forecast built from contract data rather than from account manager optimism.
recommendationReason: Renewal revenue is the largest and most predictable revenue source at this stage and is often the least rigorously forecast.

title: Standardize contract commercial terms
description: Set the standard payment terms, billing frequency, auto-renewal language, price increase clause, and termination terms, and define which deviations require approval.
outcome: A standard commercial template that protects cash flow and reduces legal review time.
recommendationReason: Non-standard payment terms negotiated deal by deal quietly extend days sales outstanding across the whole book.

title: Model consumer funnel and subscription economics
description: Model acquisition cost by channel, trial and free-to-paid conversion, subscription retention curves, refunds and chargebacks, and app store or payment processing fees.
outcome: Channel-level economics that show which acquisition spend pays back and which does not.
recommendationReason: Consumer subscription economics move quickly with channel cost and conversion, so channel-level payback must be monitored continuously.

title: Manage services margin and utilization
description: Track billable utilization, realized rate against standard rate, project margin against estimate, and the mix of services revenue relative to recurring revenue.
outcome: Services delivered at a known margin with utilization visible before the quarter ends.
recommendationReason: Service delivery margin erodes silently through scope creep and low utilization unless it is measured per project.
deliverables: Rate card and scope change policy

title: Manage inference and infrastructure cost per unit of revenue
description: Track compute and inference cost per request, per customer, and per product. Model the effect of model choice, caching, batching, and committed capacity discounts on gross margin.
outcome: A cost per unit view that lets pricing and engineering decisions be made with margin visibility.
recommendationReason: In infrastructure-heavy models, gross margin is set by engineering decisions that finance must be able to measure and price against.
deliverables: Cost per request and per customer model
Margin impact scenarios by model choice

title: Plan a price increase and customer migration
description: Design the new pricing, model revenue and churn impact by segment, set grandfathering rules, plan the communication sequence, and prepare the sales team for the conversations.
outcome: A priced and sequenced migration plan with modeled revenue impact and a churn guardrail.
recommendationReason: Price increases executed without segment modeling and a communication plan generate avoidable churn among the best customers.

title: Model partner and channel economics
description: Model the margin effect of resellers, marketplaces, and referral partners including fees, discounts, and the accounting question of gross versus net presentation.
outcome: Channel decisions made with the full margin and accounting consequences understood.
recommendationReason: Marketplace and reseller fees change both gross margin and how revenue must be presented, and both are often discovered after launch.

title: Design next year's commission plans
description: Redesign quotas, rates, accelerators, and clawbacks against the new plan targets. Model total cost of compensation and test the plan against last year's actual deal mix.
outcome: Commission plans that are modeled, affordable, and ready before the new year begins.
recommendationReason: Commission plans issued after the year starts create disputes and lose a full quarter of intended behavior change.
deliverables: Plan design with rates and accelerators
Cost model against prior year deal mix

title: Run the weekly pipeline and bookings review
description: Review pipeline coverage, stage movement, slipped deals, and bookings against target with the sales leadership team, and update the quarter forecast.
outcome: A weekly bookings forecast grounded in pipeline movement rather than in optimism.
recommendationReason: Weekly pipeline discipline is what turns a quarterly bookings target into a manageable weekly process.

title: Calculate and review commissions monthly
description: Calculate commissions from approved bookings, review exceptions, obtain sales leadership sign-off, submit to payroll, and record the accrual and any capitalized costs.
outcome: Commissions paid accurately and on time with a reviewed calculation trail.
recommendationReason: Commission errors are the fastest way for finance to lose credibility with the revenue team.

title: Run the weekly collections review
description: Work the aged receivables list, confirm promised payment dates, escalate accounts past the threshold, and apply credit holds where the policy requires it.
outcome: Aged receivables worked every week with escalations happening on schedule.
recommendationReason: Collection success falls sharply with age, so weekly contact is worth more than any policy change.

title: Review pricing performance and win-loss quarterly
description: Analyze realized price, discount trend, win rate by price point, competitive losses on price, and whether packaging changes produced the intended effect.
outcome: A quarterly evidence base for the next pricing decision.
recommendationReason: Pricing decisions made without win-loss evidence tend to repeat the same discounting behavior.

title: Review non-standard deals as they arise
description: Review any deal outside standard terms for margin, cash timing, revenue recognition, and delivery obligations before signature, and record the approval decision.
outcome: Every exception deal is reviewed and its approval recorded before signature.
recommendationReason: The exception deal is where margin, cash, and revenue timing are lost, and it is always urgent when it arrives.

title: Map the finance systems architecture
description: Draw the current architecture: source systems, integrations, direction of data flow, refresh frequency, and every point where a person moves data by hand.
outcome: A single architecture diagram showing where data breaks and where people are acting as integrations.
recommendationReason: System decisions and automation work both require a current architecture picture that usually does not exist.

title: Audit access and permissions across finance systems
description: List every user in every finance system, their permission level, whether they still need it, and whether any one person can both initiate and approve a transaction.
outcome: A cleaned access list with excessive permissions removed and conflicts documented.
recommendationReason: Excess access accumulates silently and is both the top fraud enabler and a guaranteed audit finding.

title: Inventory manual processes and critical spreadsheets
description: Catalog every recurring manual process and every spreadsheet the business depends on. Record the time it takes, who can do it, and what breaks if that person is away.
outcome: A ranked list of manual work by hours consumed and by key-person risk.
recommendationReason: Automation investment should target measured hours and concentration risk, not whatever feels most annoying.

title: Assess whether the accounting system still fits
description: Test the current system against real requirements: multi-entity, currency, revenue schedules, dimensions, approval workflow, audit trail, and integration capability. Decide whether to extend it or replace it.
outcome: A documented system decision with requirements, gap analysis, and total cost of each option.
recommendationReason: Outgrowing the accounting system shows up as spreadsheet workarounds long before anyone proposes a replacement.
deliverables: Gap analysis against the current system
Extend versus replace recommendation with costs

title: Automate the accounts payable workflow
description: Move invoice capture, coding, approval routing, and payment scheduling into a single workflow with an audit trail, and remove email-based approvals entirely.
outcome: Payables approved in a system with an audit trail rather than in email threads.
recommendationReason: Email approvals cannot be evidenced, cannot be enforced, and are the most common weak point an auditor tests first.
deliverables: Approval rules mapped to the authority matrix

title: Redesign the expense and corporate card program
description: Set spend categories and limits by role, configure card controls, define receipt requirements, automate the accounting feed, and set the review and exception process.
outcome: Card spend that posts automatically with policy enforced at the point of purchase.
recommendationReason: Enforcing spend policy at the card level is far more effective than enforcing it in a report after the money is gone.
deliverables: Card limits and controls by role

title: Build procurement and vendor intake
description: Create one intake path for new spend that captures business need, budget check, security review, legal review, and approval before a contract is signed.
outcome: New vendors enter through one reviewed path instead of arriving as an invoice.
recommendationReason: Uncontrolled vendor onboarding creates duplicate tools, unreviewed data risk, and renewals nobody planned for.

title: Assess the billing system against the pricing model
description: Test whether billing can handle the current and planned pricing: usage rating, tiers, minimums, overages, proration, credits, multi-currency, and revenue schedule output.
outcome: A billing system decision that supports the pricing the company intends to sell next year.
recommendationReason: Pricing innovation stalls when billing cannot support it, and manual invoicing does not scale past a few hundred customers.

title: Integrate payroll with the general ledger
description: Map every payroll element to accounts and departments, automate the journal entry, and build a reconciliation between payroll registers, the ledger, and tax filings.
outcome: Payroll posts automatically and reconciles to registers and filings each period.
recommendationReason: Manual payroll journals are error-prone, slow the close, and cause payroll tax reconciliation problems that surface months later.

title: Connect the equity system to accounting and payroll
description: Ensure grants, exercises, cancellations, and vesting flow to stock compensation expense and to payroll for taxable events without manual re-entry.
outcome: Equity activity flows to accounting and payroll on a defined schedule with reconciliation.
recommendationReason: Equity events that reach payroll late create tax withholding problems that are difficult and expensive to correct.

title: Establish master data governance
description: Define the system of record for customers, vendors, products, employees, and departments, set naming and identifier standards, and assign ownership for creating and changing records.
outcome: One system of record per data domain with defined ownership and change control.
recommendationReason: Reporting differences between systems almost always trace back to master data that was never governed.
deliverables: System of record decisions by domain

title: Automate bank feeds and cash application
description: Connect bank feeds to the accounting system, automate transaction matching rules, and set up automated cash application against open receivables.
outcome: Bank transactions post and match automatically with only exceptions handled by a person.
recommendationReason: Manual bank reconciliation consumes close-week hours that should go to review and analysis.

title: Implement the new accounting system
description: Run the implementation: requirements, configuration, chart of accounts and dimension setup, data migration, integration build, parallel run, user training, and cut-over.
outcome: A live accounting system with migrated history, working integrations, and a completed parallel run.
recommendationReason: System migrations at this stage are unavoidable and fail most often from weak data migration and skipped parallel testing.

title: Build the finance reporting and dashboard layer
description: Create a reporting layer over accounting, billing, customer, and payroll data with governed metric definitions, scheduled refresh, and self-service dashboards for budget owners.
outcome: Reporting that refreshes automatically from source systems using the published metric definitions.
recommendationReason: Manually built reporting packs consume the analyst capacity that should be spent on analysis.
deliverables: Refresh schedule and data quality checks

title: Implement close and reconciliation automation tooling
description: Deploy tooling for reconciliation matching, close task tracking, recurring journal automation, and flux commentary collection with review sign-off recorded in the tool.
outcome: Close tasks, reconciliations, and sign-offs tracked in one system rather than in spreadsheets and email.
recommendationReason: Close tooling produces the evidence trail auditors want while also reducing the hours the close consumes.

title: Consolidate vendors and run clean offboarding
description: Retire duplicate and unused tools with a defined offboarding checklist: data export, access removal, contract termination notice, and final invoice reconciliation.
outcome: Reduced tool spend with data exported and access removed before each contract ends.
recommendationReason: Cancelled tools that were never properly offboarded leave data behind and keep billing after the notice date.

title: Set finance document retention and file structure
description: Define where each document type lives, the folder and naming convention, the retention period, and who has access, covering contracts, workpapers, filings, and board materials.
outcome: Finance documents stored in one predictable structure with defined retention and access.
recommendationReason: Diligence and audit both consume enormous time when documents are scattered across personal drives and email.

title: Build the finance data mart in the warehouse
description: Land accounting, billing, customer, product usage, and payroll data in the warehouse with modeled tables, documented lineage, and tests that catch broken loads.
outcome: A governed finance data layer that analysis and reporting both build on.
recommendationReason: Analysis that pulls directly from source systems cannot be reproduced or reviewed, and it breaks whenever a source changes.

title: Build integration monitoring and error handling
description: Add alerting for failed syncs, record counts between systems, and a documented remediation path with a named owner for each integration.
outcome: Integration failures are detected and fixed before they reach the close.
recommendationReason: Silent integration failures are usually discovered during close, which is the most expensive time to find them.

title: Build the finance systems roadmap
description: Set the two-year systems plan: what to keep, replace, integrate, or retire, with sequencing, cost, and the capacity required to deliver it.
outcome: A sequenced systems roadmap with budget that the executive team has approved.
recommendationReason: Systems bought reactively cost more and integrate worse than systems bought against a plan.

title: Triage integration errors daily
description: Review the overnight sync results, resolve failed records, and escalate anything that cannot be fixed the same day.
outcome: Failed records are cleared daily so data stays consistent between systems.
recommendationReason: Failed integration records compound quickly and become a multi-day reconciliation exercise if left for a week.

title: Run monthly cross-system reconciliation checks
description: Reconcile record counts and totals between billing and the ledger, payroll and the ledger, the equity system and the ledger, and the expense system and the ledger.
outcome: Cross-system differences are found and explained every month before the close is locked.
recommendationReason: Systems drift apart quietly, and the difference is always harder to explain the longer it goes undetected.

title: Perform the quarterly system access review
description: Have each system owner confirm the user list and permission level, remove access for departed or moved employees, and document the review.
outcome: Documented evidence each quarter that access is appropriate and current.
recommendationReason: Access reviews are a standard control test, and quarterly evidence is far cheaper to produce than a year-end reconstruction.

title: Review vendors and renewals annually
description: Before each renewal window, review usage, license counts, pricing against market, alternatives, and whether the tool is still needed at all.
outcome: Renewals negotiated with usage data instead of accepted by default.
recommendationReason: Auto-renewal is the default outcome of not planning, and it is always more expensive than a prepared negotiation.

title: Run new system implementations to a standard playbook
description: Apply the same steps every time: requirements, security review, contract terms including data export rights, configuration, testing, training, and post-implementation review.
outcome: Every new system goes live with testing, training, and exit rights already agreed.
recommendationReason: Implementations without a standard playbook repeat the same mistakes and often omit data export rights until the exit is needed.

title: Inventory every bank account and build the daily cash position
description: List every account, institution, balance, signatory, and authorized user. Build a daily cash position report that pulls actual balances rather than ledger balances.
outcome: A complete account inventory and a working daily cash position from day one.
recommendationReason: A CFO cannot manage cash they cannot see, and forgotten accounts with stale signatories are common.

title: Rebuild the burn and runway baseline
description: Separate gross burn from net burn, isolate one-time items, compute the trailing three and six month averages, and restate runway with and without planned hiring.
outcome: A burn and runway view that separates structural burn from timing noise.
recommendationReason: Runway quoted from a single month of burn is usually wrong in the direction that feels comfortable.
deliverables: Runway scenarios with and without hiring

title: Build the 13-week cash forecast
description: Build a direct-method weekly forecast from receipts, payroll, payables runs, taxes, and known one-time items, and start tracking forecast against actual every week.
outcome: A weekly cash forecast whose accuracy is measured and improving.
recommendationReason: The 13-week direct forecast is the only cash tool that reliably shows a squeeze early enough to act.

title: Harden payment controls and update signatories
description: Update signatories and banking authority after the leadership change, require dual approval above a threshold, enable positive pay or equivalent fraud controls, and restrict wire initiation.
outcome: Payments require two people above the threshold and fraud controls are switched on at every bank.
recommendationReason: Payment fraud is the most common direct financial loss at this stage and is almost entirely preventable with bank-side controls.
deliverables: Updated signature authority at each bank

title: Build banking redundancy
description: Open and fund a second banking relationship at a different institution, keep operating balances able to cover payroll from either bank, and test that payments can actually run from the backup.
outcome: The company can make payroll from a second institution if the primary bank becomes unavailable.
recommendationReason: Concentrating all operating cash in one institution is an avoidable single point of failure for payroll.
deliverables: Second banking relationship opened and funded

title: Write and approve the investment policy
description: Set objectives in order of priority: capital preservation, liquidity, then yield. Define permitted instruments, maturity limits, concentration limits, counterparty rules, and reporting requirements.
outcome: A board-approved investment policy that governs where corporate cash may be held.
recommendationReason: Cash decisions made without a written policy tend to chase yield, and the board should set the risk tolerance explicitly.

title: Design the cash concentration and account structure
description: Decide which accounts hold operating, reserve, and invested balances, set target balances and sweep rules, and document transfer authority between them.
outcome: A deliberate account structure with defined target balances and automated sweeps.
recommendationReason: Idle balances spread across accounts earn nothing and make the cash position harder to read each morning.

title: Review outstanding debt and covenant obligations
description: Read every loan and facility agreement, extract financial and reporting covenants, build a compliance tracker, and model headroom against the current forecast.
outcome: Every covenant is tracked with modeled headroom and no reporting deadline is missed.
recommendationReason: Covenant breaches are usually foreseeable a quarter ahead, and lenders respond far better to advance notice.

title: Assess foreign currency exposure
description: Quantify exposure from foreign-currency revenue, foreign payroll, and intercompany balances. Decide whether natural offsetting is sufficient or hedging is warranted, and write the policy.
outcome: A written currency policy sized to actual exposure rather than to general anxiety.
recommendationReason: Currency exposure grows quietly with international hiring and is easiest to manage before it becomes material.

title: Standardize investor reporting
description: Set the format, metric set, and delivery date for investor updates, confirm what each financing agreement requires, and build the recurring production process.
outcome: Investor updates that go out on schedule in a consistent format that satisfies contractual requirements.
recommendationReason: Irregular investor updates create the impression of problems and make the next fundraise conversation start cold.

title: Build the capital plan and evaluate funding options
description: Model the capital required under each scenario and compare equity, venture debt, revenue-based financing, and receivables financing on cost, dilution, covenants, and time to close.
outcome: A written capital plan with the trigger point and preferred instrument for the next raise.
recommendationReason: Funding options must be evaluated while there is leverage, which is well before the cash position forces the decision.

title: Evaluate venture debt and credit facilities
description: Compare lenders on advance rate, interest, warrants, covenants, and the material adverse change clause. Model the full cost and the operating restrictions each facility imposes.
outcome: A documented decision on whether to add debt, with the full cost and restrictions understood.
recommendationReason: Venture debt is cheapest to arrange when it is not needed, and its covenants can constrain the business far more than its headline rate suggests.

title: Optimize yield within the investment policy
description: Ladder maturities against the cash forecast, compare instruments permitted by policy, and document expected yield improvement while keeping liquidity for the operating need.
outcome: Improved return on idle cash without breaching liquidity requirements or policy limits.
recommendationReason: Meaningful yield is available on operating reserves, but only with a maturity ladder built against a real cash forecast.

title: Review counterparty and deposit concentration risk
description: Assess how much cash sits at each institution relative to deposit insurance limits, review each counterparty's financial condition, and set concentration limits in policy.
outcome: Deposit and counterparty concentration measured against limits and reported to the board.
recommendationReason: Deposit concentration only becomes visible as a risk when an institution is already under stress.

title: Build and maintain the diligence data room
description: Assemble the standard diligence set: corporate records, financials, contracts, cap table, tax filings, insurance, and key policies, with a defined owner and refresh cadence.
outcome: A data room that is kept current, so a financing or acquisition process starts in days rather than weeks.
recommendationReason: Assembling a data room under deal pressure is where hidden problems are discovered by the other side first.

title: Manage the fundraising process
description: Run the raise: materials, target investor list, process calendar, diligence management, term sheet comparison, and closing mechanics alongside counsel.
outcome: A financing closed on planned terms with a controlled process and no diligence surprises.
recommendationReason: Fundraising is a full process, and a controlled one produces better terms than a reactive one.

title: Upgrade the investor relations program
description: Move beyond required reporting: structured updates, targeted asks, a warm pipeline of future investors, and consistent messaging between updates and the board deck.
outcome: Existing investors stay informed and prospective investors are already familiar before the next raise.
recommendationReason: The next round is easier when future investors have followed the story for several quarters.

title: Design global cash and subsidiary funding
description: Set how subsidiaries are funded, the intercompany loan or equity structure, repatriation constraints, and local minimum balance requirements, in coordination with tax.
outcome: A documented funding structure so subsidiaries hold the cash they need without trapping it.
recommendationReason: Cash trapped in a subsidiary through informal funding decisions is expensive and slow to release.

title: Produce the daily cash position
description: Confirm balances at every institution, record receipts and disbursements, note anything unexpected, and compare against the weekly forecast.
outcome: Cash is confirmed every business day with unexpected movements investigated the same day.
recommendationReason: Daily balance review is the primary detective control for payment fraud and bank errors.

title: Update the 13-week cash forecast weekly
description: Roll the forecast forward, load actuals, explain variance against the prior week, and flag any week where the projected balance falls below the minimum threshold.
outcome: A forecast updated weekly with measured accuracy and early warning on low-balance weeks.
recommendationReason: A cash forecast that is not updated weekly loses accuracy quickly and stops being used for decisions.

title: Report treasury position and covenant compliance monthly
description: Report balances by institution and instrument, yield earned, policy compliance, covenant calculations, and any exception requiring approval.
outcome: A monthly treasury report that evidences policy and covenant compliance.
recommendationReason: Policy and covenant compliance must be evidenced on a schedule, not asserted when someone asks.

title: Deliver the quarterly investor update
description: Publish results against plan, cash and runway, key metric movement, wins and challenges stated honestly, and the specific help being requested.
outcome: Investors receive a consistent quarterly update within the committed window.
recommendationReason: Consistent, honest updates build the credibility that shortens the next financing process.

title: Review treasury and investment policy annually
description: Reassess the policy against the current cash balance, rate environment, counterparty landscape, and business footprint, and take changes to the board for approval.
outcome: A policy that stays appropriate to the company's size and risk rather than the size it was when written.
recommendationReason: Investment policies written at an earlier cash level become either too restrictive or too permissive as the balance grows.

title: Write a decision memo for each financing action
description: For any material financing, banking, or investment action, document the alternatives considered, the recommendation, the risks, and the approval obtained.
outcome: Every material capital action has a written record of the analysis and approval behind it.
recommendationReason: Capital decisions get re-examined during diligence, and a contemporaneous memo is far more credible than a later reconstruction.

title: Inventory tax registrations, filings, and open exposure
description: List every jurisdiction where the company is registered, every filing due, the last filing made, any notices received, and any period left unfiled.
outcome: A complete filing status inventory with unfiled periods and open notices identified.
recommendationReason: Unfiled returns and unanswered notices accrue penalties silently and surface as diligence findings at the worst time.
deliverables: Registration and filing inventory by jurisdiction

title: Scan for sales tax and income tax nexus exposure
description: Map revenue, employees, contractors, and property by state against economic and physical presence thresholds. Estimate the exposure for any state where the company should have registered.
outcome: A quantified nexus exposure estimate by state with a prioritized remediation list.
recommendationReason: Sales tax exposure compounds with interest and penalties and is one of the most common material diligence findings for companies at this stage.
deliverables: Exposure estimate with interest and penalty

title: Build the tax compliance calendar
description: Create a calendar with every filing and payment obligation: federal and state income tax, estimated payments, sales and use tax, payroll tax, franchise tax, and information returns, each with an owner.
