outcome: One tax calendar with every deadline, preparer, reviewer, and filing method recorded.
recommendationReason: Missed deadlines are almost always calendar failures rather than technical failures.

title: Register for sales tax and remediate past exposure
description: Register in states where the threshold is met, evaluate voluntary disclosure agreements for past exposure, configure tax calculation in billing, and begin filing.
outcome: Sales tax collected and remitted correctly going forward with past exposure resolved on agreed terms.
recommendationReason: Voluntary disclosure typically limits the lookback period and waives penalties, but only if it happens before the state makes contact.

title: Plan federal and state income tax filings
description: Confirm the filing entity structure, the states requiring returns, apportionment methods, net operating loss positions, and estimated payment requirements, and engage a preparer.
outcome: A filing plan with the preparer engaged and the information request schedule agreed.
recommendationReason: Income tax preparation runs late whenever the state footprint and apportionment questions are answered during preparation rather than before.
deliverables: Filing plan by entity and state
Preparer engagement and information request list

title: Run the research credit study
description: Identify qualifying activities and costs, gather contemporaneous documentation, compute the credit, and decide whether to apply it against payroll tax where the company qualifies.
outcome: A documented research credit claim with the support needed to defend it on examination.
recommendationReason: The research credit is often the largest cash tax benefit available to a company at this stage, and it requires documentation captured close to the work.
deliverables: Payroll tax offset election where applicable

title: Review payroll tax registrations and remote worker states
description: Confirm the company is registered for withholding and unemployment insurance in every state where an employee works, including remote employees who moved without notice.
outcome: Payroll tax registrations complete in every state with an employee, with any gap remediated.
recommendationReason: Remote employees create payroll tax obligations in states the company never intended to enter, and the gap is usually found by a state notice.

title: Prepare income tax provision readiness
description: Build the deferred tax schedule, document the valuation allowance position, prepare the rate reconciliation, and agree the provision timeline with the auditor and the preparer.
outcome: A provision process that fits the audit timeline instead of extending it.
recommendationReason: The tax provision is a frequent cause of audit delay because it depends on nearly final numbers and outside preparers.
deliverables: Provision timeline agreed with the auditor

title: Control contractor documentation and information returns
description: Collect taxpayer identification documentation before the first payment, track reportable payments through the year, and prepare information returns on schedule.
outcome: Information returns filed accurately and on time with documentation collected up front.
recommendationReason: Chasing taxpayer identification documentation in January for a vendor paid in March is the standard avoidable annual fire drill.

title: Analyze research expenditure capitalization and cash tax impact
description: Identify research and experimental costs subject to mandatory capitalization and amortization, model the cash tax effect, and coordinate it with the research credit calculation.
outcome: A quantified cash tax impact from research expenditure treatment built into the cash forecast.
recommendationReason: Mandatory capitalization of research costs can create unexpected taxable income and a real cash tax payment for a company reporting a book loss.

title: Review state apportionment and income tax registrations
description: Determine income tax nexus by state, apply the correct apportionment method for each, register where required, and set up estimated payments.
outcome: State income tax obligations identified and registered with estimated payments scheduled.
recommendationReason: State income tax nexus rules differ from sales tax rules, so a company can be compliant on one and exposed on the other.

title: Review the international tax structure
description: Review each foreign entity for local filing obligations, permanent establishment risk, withholding tax on intercompany flows, and controlled foreign corporation reporting.
outcome: A written view of international tax obligations and risks with a remediation plan.
recommendationReason: International structures assembled to hire quickly rarely have the tax analysis done, and permanent establishment risk grows with local activity.

title: Establish transfer pricing policy and documentation
description: Define intercompany service and licensing arrangements, select and support the pricing method, execute intercompany agreements, and prepare contemporaneous documentation.
outcome: Documented and executed transfer pricing arrangements that support the intercompany charges being booked.
recommendationReason: Intercompany charges without agreements and documentation are challenged in examinations and flagged in diligence.

title: Assess international indirect tax obligations
description: Determine value added tax and goods and services tax registration thresholds in each country of sale, configure tax determination in billing, and set up local filing.
outcome: International indirect tax registered, calculated in billing, and filed on the local calendar.
recommendationReason: International indirect tax obligations are triggered by customer location rather than company location and are commonly missed until a customer asks for a compliant invoice.

title: Run annual tax planning and elections
description: Review available elections, credit utilization, net operating loss planning, entity structure changes, and any transaction with tax consequences before the year closes.
outcome: Tax planning decisions made and elections filed before the deadlines that make them available.
recommendationReason: Most tax elections are only available prospectively or by a fixed date, so planning after year end forfeits the option.

title: File sales and use tax returns
description: Prepare returns from billing data, reconcile collected tax to the liability account, remit payment, and confirm each filing was accepted.
outcome: Sales tax returns filed and reconciled every period with acceptance confirmed.
recommendationReason: Sales tax collected but not remitted is held in trust for the state, and shortfalls carry personal liability risk in many jurisdictions.

title: Calculate and pay quarterly estimated taxes
description: Estimate taxable income for federal and state purposes, compute required payments including safe harbor amounts, and pay before each deadline.
outcome: Estimated payments made on time in the right amount, avoiding underpayment penalties.
recommendationReason: Underpayment penalties are avoidable with a safe harbor calculation and a calendar reminder.

title: Manage the annual income tax return cycle
description: Assemble the information request package, review draft returns, confirm book-to-tax differences, file or extend on time, and reconcile to the provision.
outcome: Returns filed or properly extended with book-to-tax differences documented.
recommendationReason: Return preparation runs late when the information package is assembled after the request arrives rather than before.

title: Assess tax obligations before entering a new jurisdiction
description: Before hiring in a new state or country or selling into one, determine registration, withholding, indirect tax, and entity requirements and the cost of compliance.
outcome: Jurisdiction entry decisions made with the compliance cost and obligations known in advance.
recommendationReason: It is far cheaper to register correctly before the first employee or first sale than to remediate afterwards.

title: Respond to tax notices on a defined protocol
description: Log every notice on receipt, assess the deadline and exposure, respond within the required window, and track it to closure with written confirmation.
outcome: No tax notice goes unanswered past its deadline and each is tracked to written closure.
recommendationReason: Unanswered notices escalate to assessments and liens, and they are frequently lost in a shared mailbox.

title: Review payment and fraud exposure immediately
description: Test the current payment path end to end: who can initiate, who approves, how vendor bank details are changed, and whether any bank-side fraud controls are switched on.
outcome: Immediate closure of any path that lets one person move money alone or change vendor bank details unchecked.
recommendationReason: Vendor bank detail changes and single-approver wires are the two mechanisms behind most payment fraud losses at this stage.

title: Build the enterprise risk register
description: Collect risks from every function, score them on likelihood and impact, assign an owner and a current mitigation to each, and identify the risks with no mitigation at all.
outcome: A ranked risk register with a named owner for each of the top risks.
recommendationReason: Risks that are known informally by individual leaders are never managed as a portfolio until they are written down together.

title: Publish the delegation of authority matrix
description: Define approval limits by transaction type and amount for purchases, contracts, hiring, payments, pricing exceptions, and capital commitments, up to the board threshold.
outcome: One published matrix that defines who can commit the company to what.
recommendationReason: Without published limits, spending authority is assumed rather than granted, and the board's reserved matters are unclear.

title: Review segregation of duties
description: Map who can initiate, approve, record, and reconcile in each financial process. Identify conflicts and add compensating controls where the team is too small to fully separate duties.
outcome: Documented duty conflicts with either separation or an explicit compensating control.
recommendationReason: Small finance teams cannot fully separate duties, so conflicts must be identified and compensated deliberately rather than ignored.

title: Harden bank and payment platform controls
description: Enable positive pay and account validation services, restrict payment file upload rights, set transaction limits, and require callback verification for any bank detail change.
outcome: Bank-side controls that stop fraudulent payments before they leave the account.
recommendationReason: Bank-provided fraud tools stop losses that internal approval processes cannot, and they are usually not enabled by default.

title: Document the key controls matrix
description: For each significant process, document the risk, the control that addresses it, the control owner, the frequency, and the evidence the control produces.
outcome: A control matrix that maps risks to controls and to the evidence each one leaves behind.
recommendationReason: Controls that produce no evidence cannot be tested, and controls that are not mapped to a risk usually should not exist.

title: Build the third-party risk program
description: Tier vendors by data sensitivity and business criticality, require security documentation at the appropriate tier, review contract protections, and track review dates.
outcome: Vendors reviewed proportionally to the risk they carry, with evidence retained.
recommendationReason: Vendor data breaches and vendor failures become the company's problem, and diligence increasingly asks how vendors were assessed.

title: Build the finance business continuity plan
description: Document how payroll, payments, billing, and close would run if a key system, a key person, or a bank became unavailable, and test at least one scenario.
outcome: A tested continuity plan for the finance processes that cannot stop.
recommendationReason: Payroll and payments have no acceptable outage window, so the fallback must exist and be tested before it is needed.

title: Establish the whistleblower and ethics channel
description: Set up an anonymous reporting channel, define who receives reports, document the investigation process, and confirm the non-retaliation policy is communicated.
outcome: A working confidential reporting channel with a documented investigation and escalation path.
recommendationReason: A confidential channel is a standard governance expectation and a practical early warning mechanism for financial misconduct.

title: Launch the control testing program
description: Select the controls to test, define sample sizes and testing methods, perform the testing, document exceptions, and track remediation to closure.
outcome: Evidence that key controls operate, with exceptions tracked and closed.
recommendationReason: A documented control that has never been tested provides no assurance to the board or to an auditor.

title: Build lightweight control readiness for future reporting requirements
description: Assess the control environment against public company expectations, identify the largest gaps, and build a phased plan so remediation is spread over years rather than months.
outcome: A phased readiness plan that avoids a compressed and expensive remediation later.
recommendationReason: Control remediation done under a public offering timeline costs several times more than the same work done gradually.

title: Align finance with security and privacy programs
description: Coordinate with security on access governance, data classification for financial data, incident notification to finance, and the finance evidence needed for security certifications.
outcome: Finance controls and security controls that reinforce each other and produce shared evidence.
recommendationReason: Security certifications require finance controls as evidence, and duplicated effort is avoidable when the programs are aligned.

title: Audit expense and travel spend
description: Test a sample of expense reports against policy, look for split transactions, duplicate submissions, and personal spend, and report findings with recommended policy changes.
outcome: Evidence of whether the expense policy is followed and where the controls need to change.
recommendationReason: Expense abuse is rarely large individually but signals whether policy is taken seriously across the company.

title: Build the annual internal audit plan
description: Select review areas based on the risk register, decide what is done internally versus by an outside firm, set the schedule, and agree reporting to the audit committee.
outcome: A risk-based audit plan approved by the board or audit committee.
recommendationReason: Reviews chosen by risk find more than reviews chosen by convenience, and the plan should be visible to the board.

title: Set controls for artificial intelligence tool usage in finance
description: Define which finance data may be used with which tools, require human review of generated output that affects the books, and log where automated tools touch financial processes.
outcome: Clear rules on tool usage with financial data and a record of where automation touches the books.
recommendationReason: Finance teams adopt these tools quickly, and confidential data exposure or unreviewed output in the ledger are both realistic failure modes.
deliverables: Tool usage policy for financial data
Human review requirement for material output

title: Review control exceptions monthly
description: Review exceptions raised during the month: approval overrides, manual journal entries above threshold, access changes, and payment exceptions, and confirm each was justified.
outcome: Exceptions are reviewed while they can still be corrected and patterns are visible early.
recommendationReason: Isolated exceptions look reasonable individually, and only a monthly review reveals a pattern of override.

title: Review the risk register quarterly
description: Reassess likelihood and impact, retire resolved risks, add new ones, confirm owners, and report the top risks and their movement to the board.
outcome: A current risk register reviewed with the board each quarter.
recommendationReason: A risk register that is not reviewed becomes a historical document within two quarters.

title: Review duty separation and authority limits quarterly
description: Confirm that role changes, departures, and new systems have not created new duty conflicts, and that approval limits still match the current organization.
outcome: Duty conflicts introduced by organizational change are found within the quarter.
recommendationReason: Every reorganization and departure quietly changes who can do what, and nobody notices until a review is scheduled.

title: Run the annual fraud risk assessment
description: Consider fraud scenarios across revenue, payments, payroll, expense, and financial reporting, evaluate the controls addressing each, and address the gaps.
outcome: A documented annual fraud assessment with the identified gaps assigned and closed.
recommendationReason: Structured fraud scenario analysis finds gaps that process-based control reviews miss.

title: Respond to financial incidents on a defined protocol
description: For any suspected fraud, payment error, data incident, or control failure, follow the protocol: contain, quantify, notify, investigate, remediate, and document.
outcome: Incidents are handled consistently with a written record and a completed remediation.
recommendationReason: The first hours of an incident determine recoverability, and improvisation costs both money and evidence.

title: Baseline headcount, payroll, and employee locations
description: Reconcile the human resources system to payroll and to the ledger, confirm every employee's work location and classification, and identify anyone paid outside the payroll system.
outcome: An accurate headcount and payroll baseline with work locations confirmed for every employee.
recommendationReason: Headcount reported by people operations, payroll, and the ledger usually differ, and location errors create tax exposure.

title: Verify the capitalization table
description: Reconcile the cap table to board consents, stock purchase agreements, option grants, exercises, cancellations, and financing documents, and resolve every difference.
outcome: A cap table that agrees to the underlying legal documents with all differences resolved.
recommendationReason: Cap table errors compound at each financing and are extremely expensive and embarrassing to fix during a round.
deliverables: Cap table reconciliation to source documents

title: Build the workforce plan and hiring tracker
description: Build an approved position list with role, level, location, target start date, and fully loaded cost, and track every open requisition against it.
outcome: One approved headcount plan that recruiting, hiring managers, and finance all work from.
recommendationReason: Hiring drifts beyond plan when approved positions are tracked by recruiting rather than against the budget.
deliverables: Requisition tracker linked to the budget

title: Establish payroll controls and approvals
description: Require documented approval for new hires, pay changes, bonuses, and terminations, add a pre-transmission review of the payroll register, and separate the person who enters changes from the person who approves the run.
outcome: Payroll runs only after a reviewed register and documented approval for every change.
recommendationReason: Payroll is the largest recurring cash outflow, and unreviewed changes are both an error and a fraud risk.
deliverables: Duty separation in the payroll system

title: Review compensation bands and pay equity
description: Compare current pay against market data by role, level, and location, identify outliers and internal inconsistencies, and cost the plan to bring people into band.
outcome: A costed compensation structure with outliers identified and a plan to address them.
recommendationReason: Ad hoc compensation decisions create internal inconsistency that becomes expensive and difficult to unwind at scale.
deliverables: Band structure by role and level
Cost to bring people into band

title: Standardize the equity grant process
description: Define grant guidelines by role and level, the approval path through the board, the timing of grants relative to the valuation, and how grants are communicated and documented.
outcome: Equity granted on a schedule with board approval documented before the grant date.
recommendationReason: Grants promised in offer letters but approved by the board weeks later create valuation and compliance problems.
deliverables: Grant guidelines by role and level

title: Model the option pool and dilution
description: Project pool consumption against the hiring plan, model refresh grants, and show founder and investor dilution under different pool increase and financing scenarios.
outcome: A dilution model that shows when the pool runs out and what an increase costs existing holders.
recommendationReason: Pool exhaustion is discovered mid-hire without a model, and pool increases negotiated during a financing are more dilutive.

title: Refresh the 409A valuation
description: Engage a qualified valuation provider, supply the required financial and forecast information, review the draft, and obtain board approval of the resulting strike price.
outcome: A current valuation supporting the strike price on all new grants.
recommendationReason: Grants issued on a stale valuation create tax exposure for employees and a correction problem for the company.
deliverables: Board approval of the strike price

title: Review contractor and employee classification
description: Test each contractor relationship against the applicable classification tests, quantify the exposure of any misclassification, and convert or restructure where needed.
outcome: Worker classifications reviewed and documented with misclassification risk addressed.
recommendationReason: Long-term full-time contractors are a common and costly classification exposure, especially across multiple states and countries.

title: Model international employment cost and structure
description: Model the fully loaded cost of employment in each country including employer contributions, statutory benefits, notice periods, and severance, and compare employer of record cost with running a local entity.
outcome: A cost comparison that supports where and how to hire internationally.
recommendationReason: Fully loaded international employment cost frequently exceeds the domestic assumption used in the hiring plan.
deliverables: Employer of record versus entity comparison

title: Review benefits and total rewards cost
description: Analyze benefit cost per employee, utilization, renewal increases, and plan design alternatives, and model the effect of design changes on cost and on employee value.
outcome: A benefits decision supported by cost, utilization, and market comparison data.
recommendationReason: Benefits renewals often carry double-digit increases that are accepted without analysis or alternative quotes.
deliverables: Plan design options with cost impact

title: Assess the payroll and human resources platform
description: Test the provider against multi-state and multi-country requirements, accounting integration quality, reporting, tax filing accuracy, and support responsiveness.
outcome: A documented decision to keep or replace the payroll platform based on tested requirements.
recommendationReason: Payroll providers that worked at an earlier scale often cannot handle multi-state and multi-country complexity or provide usable accounting output.

title: Design the equity refresh and retention program
description: Define refresh grant guidelines, evergreen and performance grant treatment, promotion grants, and model the pool and expense impact over the next three years.
outcome: A retention equity program with modeled pool consumption and expense impact.
recommendationReason: Early employees approach the end of their vesting schedules at this stage, and retention equity needs a plan rather than case-by-case decisions.

title: Decide employer of record versus local entity by country
description: For each country with employees, compare the ongoing cost, compliance obligations, intellectual property protection, and flexibility of an employer of record against establishing a local entity.
outcome: A documented country-by-country decision with a transition plan where an entity is warranted.
recommendationReason: Employer of record arrangements are the right first step but become expensive and limiting once several employees are in one country.

title: Support the annual compensation cycle
description: Build the compensation budget, model merit, promotion, and equity refresh scenarios against the plan, and provide the tooling and guardrails managers need to allocate within budget.
outcome: A funded compensation cycle that lands within the approved budget and the approved bands.
recommendationReason: Compensation cycles run without a modeled budget consistently exceed plan and force reductions elsewhere.

title: Review and sign off payroll each cycle
description: Compare the register against the prior period, investigate every change, confirm approvals exist for new hires, terminations, and pay changes, and sign off before transmission.
outcome: Every payroll is reviewed against the prior period and signed off before it is transmitted.
recommendationReason: Period-over-period payroll comparison is the single most effective detective control against payroll error and fraud.

title: Reconcile headcount to plan monthly
description: Compare actual headcount against the approved plan by department, explain differences, update the forecast for hiring delays, and flag positions filled without approval.
outcome: Headcount actuals reconciled to plan every month with hiring pace reflected in the forecast.
recommendationReason: Headcount is the largest driver of expense variance, and hiring delays change runway more than any other single input.
deliverables: Hiring pace update to the forecast

title: Reconcile the cap table quarterly
description: Reconcile grants, exercises, cancellations, and repurchases to board approvals and to the stock compensation expense schedule, and confirm the fully diluted count.
outcome: A cap table that continuously agrees to board approvals and to the accounting records.
recommendationReason: Quarterly reconciliation keeps the cap table clean, so a financing or diligence request never triggers a clean-up project.

title: Run the annual valuation and equity compliance cycle
description: Refresh the 409A valuation on schedule or after a material event, complete required employee equity tax filings and notices, and confirm plan share reserves remain sufficient.
outcome: Valuation and equity compliance obligations completed on time every year.
recommendationReason: Valuations expire and equity notice obligations recur annually, and both are easy to miss without a scheduled cycle.
deliverables: Completed equity tax filings and notices

title: Process new hires and terminations to checklist
description: For each hire and departure, complete the finance checklist: payroll setup or removal, equity grant or post-termination exercise handling, system access, equipment, and final pay calculation.
outcome: Every hire and departure is processed against a checklist with nothing left open.
recommendationReason: Incomplete termination processing leaves active system access and unresolved equity questions that become disputes.
deliverables: Final pay and equity treatment record

title: Review board minutes, consents, and corporate records
description: Read the minute book and confirm that every financing, option grant, plan increase, officer appointment, and major contract has the board approval it required.
outcome: A record of which corporate actions lack proper approval documentation, with a clean-up plan.
recommendationReason: Missing consents are found during financing diligence, when they are slow and expensive to remedy.

title: Confirm entity standing and registrations
description: Verify good standing for every entity in its state or country of formation, confirm foreign qualifications where the company does business, and check registered agent details.
outcome: Every entity confirmed in good standing with any lapsed registration identified.
recommendationReason: Lapsed good standing blocks financings and contract signatures and is usually discovered at the worst moment.

title: Inventory insurance policies and coverage
description: List every policy with limits, deductibles, exclusions, renewal date, and broker. Compare coverage against the company's actual risk profile and any contractual insurance requirements.
outcome: A coverage summary showing gaps against both risk and customer contract requirements.
recommendationReason: Insurance bought at an earlier stage is frequently below the limits customer contracts now require.
deliverables: Policy inventory with limits and exclusions

title: Publish the board calendar and approval requirements
description: Set meeting dates for the year, define the material deadlines for each meeting, and document which decisions require board or stockholder approval under the charter and financing agreements.
outcome: A published calendar and a clear list of decisions that cannot be made without board approval.
recommendationReason: Board approval requirements sit across several documents, and actions are taken without approval when nobody has consolidated them.
deliverables: Board meeting calendar with material deadlines
Reserved matters and approval requirement list

title: Handle franchise tax and annual report filings
description: Confirm the calculation method that produces the correct franchise tax, file annual reports for every entity, and calendar all recurring corporate filings.
outcome: Franchise tax and annual reports filed correctly and on time for every entity.
recommendationReason: Franchise tax calculated on the default method is frequently far higher than the alternative method allows.

title: Define the finance interface to contracting
description: Agree which contracts finance must review before signature, what finance checks for, where executed contracts are stored, and how key commercial terms reach billing and accounting.
outcome: A defined review path so commercial terms reach billing and accounting without being re-read from the contract.
recommendationReason: Contract terms that never reach finance become billing errors, revenue recognition issues, and missed obligations.

title: Review directors and officers insurance
description: Assess limits against company stage, board composition, and financing activity. Review the definition of insured persons, the exclusions, and the tail coverage provisions.
outcome: Coverage appropriate to the current board and financing profile with exclusions understood.
recommendationReason: Directors expect adequate coverage, and limits set at an earlier stage rarely match a larger board and a larger balance sheet.

title: Assess cyber and technology liability coverage
description: Review cyber liability and technology errors and omissions coverage against the data held, the contractual commitments made to customers, and realistic incident cost.
outcome: Cyber and technology coverage sized to the data risk and to customer contract requirements.
recommendationReason: Customer contracts increasingly specify minimum cyber coverage, and incident costs exceed limits set at earlier stages.

title: Establish board committee structure
description: Set up audit and compensation committees with written charters, defined membership, meeting cadence, and the materials finance must prepare for each.
outcome: Functioning committees with charters and a defined materials package for each meeting.
recommendationReason: Committees create the governance structure investors expect and move detailed review out of the full board meeting.

title: Align the equity plan with board consent practice
description: Confirm plan share reserves, the grant approval mechanism, consent templates, and the timing between offer, board approval, and grant date.
outcome: Equity grants approved and documented correctly with sufficient shares reserved.
recommendationReason: Grants documented incorrectly or approved after the fact create tax problems for employees and clean-up work for the company.

title: Review the entity structure for rationalization
description: Assess whether every entity is still needed, what each one costs annually to maintain, and whether dormant entities should be dissolved or merged.
outcome: A decision on which entities to keep, dissolve, or merge with the annual cost of each.
recommendationReason: Dormant entities carry filing, tax, and audit cost every year and add work to every diligence exercise.

title: Prepare international entity readiness
description: For each country where an entity is warranted, map the formation requirements, local director and registered office obligations, statutory accounts, local audit thresholds, and ongoing filing cost.
outcome: A country readiness pack showing what establishing and running an entity actually requires.
recommendationReason: Local statutory accounts, director requirements, and audit thresholds are routinely underestimated when entities are set up quickly.

title: Build the policy library and attestation process
description: Consolidate finance and company policies in one place, set a review owner and cycle for each, and run annual employee attestation for the policies that require it.
outcome: A single current policy library with recorded employee attestations.
recommendationReason: Policies scattered across documents and drives cannot be enforced, and attestation evidence is a standard diligence request.
deliverables: Policy library with owners and review dates

title: Scan for regulatory and licensing obligations
description: Identify any licensing, registration, or sector-specific regulation triggered by the products sold, the data handled, the customers served, or the jurisdictions entered.
outcome: A documented view of regulatory obligations with owners for any that apply.
recommendationReason: Regulatory obligations are triggered by product and customer changes that finance often learns about after launch.

title: Refresh the annual governance calendar
description: Rebuild the calendar for the coming year: board and committee meetings, annual stockholder consent, entity filings, insurance renewals, policy reviews, and valuation refresh.
outcome: A complete governance calendar for the next year with owners assigned to every obligation.
recommendationReason: Governance obligations are annual and easy to miss when they are tracked in several separate places.
deliverables: Governance calendar for the coming year

title: Run the insurance renewal strategy
description: Start renewals early, prepare complete underwriting submissions, obtain competing quotes, and negotiate limits and terms against the current risk profile rather than last year's.
outcome: Renewals completed on better terms because the submission was prepared and the market was tested.
recommendationReason: Insurance renewals negotiated in the final weeks produce worse terms than renewals prepared months ahead.

title: Prepare and run the quarterly board meeting
description: Build the agenda, prepare and circulate materials in advance, prepare consents for items requiring approval, and produce minutes promptly after the meeting.
outcome: Board meetings run to agenda with approvals documented and minutes finalized quickly.
recommendationReason: Approvals that are discussed but never documented in minutes or consents do not exist for diligence purposes.

title: Review contractual obligations monthly
description: Review upcoming contract renewals, notice deadlines, service commitments, and any obligation with a financial consequence approaching in the next ninety days.
outcome: Contract deadlines are acted on before automatic renewal or breach.
recommendationReason: Notice periods pass silently and convert into another year of commitment nobody chose.

title: Complete annual entity filings for every entity
description: File annual reports, pay franchise and registration fees, confirm registered agent details, and hold or document the annual stockholder actions required.
outcome: Every entity remains in good standing with all annual filings completed on time.
recommendationReason: Missed annual filings result in loss of good standing, penalties, and blocked transactions.

title: Process board approval requests as they arise
description: When an action requires board approval, prepare the decision memo, obtain the consent or place it on the agenda, and file the executed documentation in the minute book.
outcome: Every action requiring board approval is documented before the action is taken.
recommendationReason: Approvals obtained after the fact are a governance defect that surfaces in every diligence review.
